rearConcept.method: Qwen Scene mode repainting an orthographic back render of the approved mesh, with the front concept as identity reference

materials.provenance: Base colour re-baked (Cycles CPU, emission, selected-to-active) from the approved source mesh, whose back carries the approved rear-view concept projection; tangent normals baked from the source geometry and whiteout-blended with colour relief; AO baked from the decimated geometry; roughness, metalness and dye mask derived from colour inside declared regions. Base colour then lifted by luma power toneGamma after the repairs (chroma ratios kept), calibrated in the game against the approved concept. Artistic derivation, not measured PBR.
materials.toneCalibration: Luma power fitted in the game to lift the resident's mean luma from the default follow camera (world yaw pi, pitch 0.48, 18 and 26 m, 8 facings, high and low quality, resident-only pixels) toward the approved TRELLIS input's foreground mean luma (50.6/255). The concept is out of reach at the 0.6 floor, the strongest power measured: about 49.0/255; 23.5/255 as cooked without it.

toneCalibration.method: Mean Rec.709 luma (0-255) of the resident's own pixels in the game presenter (both qualities, 18 and 26 m, 8 facings, default follow camera at world yaw pi and pitch 0.48), each rendered over two backgrounds with every other drawable hidden; the concept value is the alpha-masked TRELLIS input. toneGamma was interpolated between measured powers (1, 0.85, 0.72, 0.6) to meet the concept, and floored at 0.6, the strongest power measured.
toneCalibration.note: The concept is out of reach at the 0.6 floor; the resident stays slightly darker than its concept.

baseEncoding.reason: Base-colour alpha is the dye mask; libwebp's default lossy mode discards RGB under alpha 0.

cook.scriptsNote: SHA-256 of each script with LF line endings, equal to its copy in scripts/models/pipeline.
cook.verification: tests/resident-models.test.ts verifies every 60 Hz frame of Idle and Talk as planted loops and rejects six deliberately broken copies; tests/residents-browser.test.ts renders the residents in the game's WebGL presenter.

limitations: Single-view TRELLIS reconstruction: hands are fused 'mitten' shapes and the face is soft, with smeared eye sockets; at the game's closest camera (18 m) a resident is about 140 px tall, so neither reads in play.

The back is a projected rear-view concept (Qwen repainting an orthographic back render of the approved mesh, with the front concept as identity reference), blended into the reconstructed texture at the sides; the nearest painted colour fills the few back pixels the painting does not reach.
Roughness, metalness and ambient occlusion are derived from colour inside declared regions and Cycles bakes, not measured PBR or hand-painted masks.
Linear blend skinning with shoulder and knee helpers and hem panels; edge strain is bounded on every 60 Hz frame (the provenance records the measured maxima).

Two procedural loops authored in Blender, Idle and Talk, with no motion capture, no facial animation, no lip sync, no finger animation and no cloth simulation; clips are keyed at 30 Hz. Residents stand: there is no walk, turn or work clip, and the presenter turns them to face the hero instantly, as the procedural figures did.
Re-cooking is not guaranteed to be byte-reproducible: MikkTSpace tangents can round differently on a few vertices.

The shawl is fused to the arms; weights are relaxed across the torso and arms to keep it from tearing, and the strain is the closest of the five to the limits (worst crush 0.04x against 0.02x, 99.5th-percentile stretch 1.938x against 2.0x, both in Talk).
From behind, the skirt reads plum-red against the front's dark brown; tone stops at the 0.6 floor (49.0 against 50.6), and the lift turns the tan boots orange.
